title: Ambient session surface — proto memo
body:
TL;DR: Sketch for an 'ambient session surface' — lightweight UI + API pattern to surface short-lived context, suggested next actions, and cost/fidelity controls to end users and integrators. Purpose: reduce token waste, improve perceived responsiveness, and make fallback decisions explicit to product devs.

Problem space:
- Many apps keep full conversation state always-on; cost and latency grow with long histories.
- Users and engineers lack a compact, actionable representation of session health (how much context is being sent, when we switch to cheap model, etc.).
- Rollouts for progressive fidelity often feel opaque — developers want a simple knob and preview.

Hypothesis:
- Exposing a small session surface (3–5 lines) + a fidelity slider + 'cost impact' estimate will reduce token usage by ~15–30% for chat-style apps without hurting NPS.

Primary personas:
- Product engineer (wants predictable unit economics + easy integration)
- End user (wants faster answers and clarity when model did a shortcut)
- Platform operator (needs observability for rollout SLOs)

User journeys (quick):
1) New user opens assistant: ambient surface shows 3-line recap + suggestion buttons (ask to expand, show source, reduce fidelity).
2) Power user toggles fidelity to get full detail (switches to higher-cost model for a single request).
3) App developer pins a prompt chunk as 'sticky' from the surface to guarantee availability across cheap plan.

Rough user stories:
- As a product engineer, I can opt-in to ambientSurface=true in the API so the response includes a compact recap and cost estimate.
- As an end user, I can tap 'expand' to get the full context the model saw, with an indicator if the request used a fallback.
- As a platform operator, I can query per-session token counts and per-surface toggles for billing and SLO reporting.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- API returns 'ambient_surface' object with: one-sentence recap, 3 bullet highlights, token_count_estimate, fallback_flag. (UI can mock.)
- Console UI shows ambient surface under route -> model -> session flows and exposes per-session toggle.
- Metrics emitted: ambient.surface.rendered, ambient.surface.expand_click, ambient.surface.fidelity_override.

Success metrics (first 8 weeks):
- Reduction in median tokens per session by 15% (target).
- <1% increase in error rate after rollout.
- Developer adoption: 20+ teams test flag in sandbox.

Experiments & rollout approach:
- Phase A: server-side only; API adds ambient_surface payload when flag set. Collect telemetry, no client UI. (2 weeks)
- Phase B: optional client-side UI in console + sample web widget; invite 5 pilot teams. (3–4 weeks)
- Phase C: public SDK support + 'fidelity slider' in console; measure cost impact and UX. (4 weeks)

Implementation notes (cheap sketch):
- Generation: ambient_surface produced by a small extractive model (or distilled head) that summarizes last N user/assistant turns and tags sticky prompts. Option to use cached prefix summary for long sessions.
- Token estimate: use same tokenizer as runtime; estimate request total if ambient is included vs full history.
- Flags: per-route config: ambient_mode {off, readonly, interactive}.

Open questions / risks:
- Summaries could hallucinate; need clear UI label "system-generated recap" and quick expand to full context.
- Extra compute to generate surface might negate cost savings if not cached. Tradeoff: run summary generation asynchronously and cache for 30–90s.
- Privacy/PII: exposing expanded context in UI may leak; require redaction filter for console and widget.

Quick UX constraints (notes-to-self):
- Keep surface <3 lines by default, collapse on mobile.
- Provide 'why did model respond like this' tooltip linking to fallback/mode.

Next steps (short):
- Prototype server-side ambient_surface payload (INF-3421 spike). Owner: Amrita. ETA: 2w.
- Hook minimal telemetry; add metric counters listed above. Owner: Leo. ETA: 1w.
- Design quick console mockups and a sample widget. Owner: Maya. ETA: 2w.

Unresolved TODOs:
- Decide distillation vs extractive generation approach for summaries (bench cost / latency).
- Add redaction filter: list PII dims to scrub before surface generation.
- Flesh out API contract (field names + rate limits).

Notes to self: keep this light — the thing that will make people use it is clarity about cost impact and a simple integration path (one flag + opt-in client).

References/links in thread: JIRA INF-3421, Slack #sess-ux (ambient-surface-proto), GH PR: ux-prototypes/pull/78
